problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $2\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(3,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the acceleration of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{6}$ seconds.

feedback.problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $3\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(4,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the acceleration of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{3}$ seconds.
feedback.worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $a$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=a(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and the particle is at the position $(a,0)$ when $t=0.$

In our case, we have $a=4$ and $\omega =3\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =4(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity and acceleration vectors by differentiating. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(4(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-12\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,i+12\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,j \\ a(t) & =(-12\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,i+12\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-36\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,i-36\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the acceleration vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{3},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\frac{\pi }{3}) & =-36\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{3})\,i-36\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{3})\,j \\  & =-36\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )\,i-36\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )\,j \\  & =36\,i\end{aligned}
$$
